messages.subject: geom_bar() question
parts:
Hello -

I would like to make a barplot. I input the data in 2 variables, a and b

a <- c('pop1', 'pop1', 'pop2', 'pop2', 'pop3', 'pop3')
b <- c(21.85, 9.66, 17.43, 12.92, 3.56, 6.03)

library(ggplot2)

qplot(factor(a), geom='bar', fill=factor(b))

The result looks like: www.crypticlineage.net/rdisc/temp.png

There are 2 problems with this. There should be a total of only three
colors in there, one per population. The bars should be scaled by
vector b values.

So I made a third vector, c

c <- c('pop2', 'pop3', 'pop1', 'pop3', 'pop1', 'pop2')

qplot(factor(a), geom='bar', fill=factor(c))

Result is here: www.crypticlineage.net/rdisc/temp2.png

Now the colors are correct. However, now I don't know how to bring in
vector 'b'.

Thanks for all the help.

V

messages.subject: Re: geom_bar() question
parts:
Hi,

Thanks, that makes it somewhat clearer. I still find the example
confusing though. If you put these three variables together in a
data.frame, you get

> dat <- data.frame(a = a, b=b, c=c)
> dat
a b c
1 pop1 21.85 pop2
2 pop1 9.66 pop3
3 pop2 17.43 pop1
4 pop2 12.92 pop3
5 pop3 3.56 pop1
6 pop3 6.03 pop2

so is row 1 pop1 or pop2? Of course this doesn't really matter in
terms of plotting it:

ggplot(dat, aes(x = a, y = b, fill = c)) + geom_bar(stat="identity")

HTH,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: geom_bar() question
parts:
Hi Ista,

To make my example clearer, I have three populations and I am
measuring gene flow between pairs of populations.

So, pop1 receives geneflow from pop2 and pop3
pop2 from pop1 and pop3 and finally,
pop3 from pop1 and pop2.

The numbers of the estimates of gene flow.

Following your data.frame example, this graph was created:

www.crypticlineage.net/rdisc/temp4.png

However, there is a problem with it. For every population on x axis,
ggplot is adding up gene flow from both contributing populations to
construct the length of graph. For example, in FR population, RH
contributes to 17.43, GL contributes 12.92. So the bar height is
17.43+12.92 = ~30. However, I want the bar height to be 17.43 and a
horizontal mark at 12.92. Does this make sense?

Moreover, I would also like to shrink the width of the bars and place
labels for contributing populations on the bars. I tried
aes(label=c), but, that placed labels in inaccurate positions.

Thanks again
Vikram
